faq.q: Which invisible character does it insert, and does the choice matter?
faq.a: You pick one of three: a zero-width space (U+200B), a Braille blank (U+2800) or an invisible separator (U+2063). Each blank line in your text is replaced with that character so the gap survives when the platform strips empty lines. The hint under the options notes the Braille blank may show as a faint dot in some fonts, and support for the separator varies by app.

faq.q: What does the character counter check against?
faq.a: It counts the formatted output against the limit for the platform you select: Instagram caption 2,200, Instagram bio 150, TikTok 2,200, Twitter/X 280, LinkedIn 3,000, Facebook 63,206 or YouTube description 5,000. It shows characters used, the limit and how many are left, turning red if you go over. Note the invisible spacing characters count toward that total.

faq.q: How does the Fancy Text tab work — is it a real font?
faq.a: It maps your letters to Unicode variants (Bold, Italic, Script, Double-struck, Monospace, Circled, Squared, Small Caps and Upside Down), so it's not a font but actual different characters that paste anywhere. It converts either your whole caption or just the selection highlighted in the Spacer box. Because they're special Unicode, screen readers may read them oddly.

faq.q: Can I add hashtags without cluttering the caption?
faq.a: Yes. In the Hashtags tab, tick 'Move hashtags to end with spacing' and Append adds them after three dotted spacer lines, or use 'Copy as First Comment' to paste them as the first comment instead. There are also caption templates (hook+value+CTA, story, product, quote, carousel) and an emoji/divider inserter. Your last five captions are autosaved.
